Works with

Rugged tablet for WorkPal

WorkPal is job management software from WorkPal Limited of Belfast, which describes it as the all-in-one job management software built to streamline your business from quote to cash. The industries listed on its site are cleaning management, drainage, electrical, environmental services, facilities management, fire and security, landscaping and grounds maintenance, pest control, plumbing and HVAC, property maintenance, roofing, and salting and gritting. The vendor's supported countries page says the system is accessible from the United Kingdom and Ireland among a list of 32 countries. The office works in a desktop web platform; field staff use the WorkPal mobile app, which has its own login and licence.

The mobile app is where the day's work is recorded. The vendor's mobile user guide describes starting a shift, which records working time and enables location tracking, travelling to a job with directions and travel timers, then on site adding notes, attaching read-only PDFs such as safety certificates or site plans, completing forms, taking photos or choosing them from the gallery, and finishing with an operative signature and, where required, a customer signature. The vendor says the app works without an internet connection and syncs when the connection returns, with an Outbox counter that shows what is still waiting. All of that happens in plant rooms, loft spaces, drains, gardens and vans, where a consumer tablet tends to crack, fog up or run flat before the shift ends.

This page sets out what WorkPal publishes about the devices its app runs on, what it does not publish, which Tuga rugged devices meet the published requirement, and how a UK field team can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet. Nothing here is a vendor endorsement: check your own WorkPal account on the device during the 30-day returns window.

Requirements

What WorkPal needs from a device

Each item below comes from WorkPal Limited's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 11 or later, from Google Play, on phones and tablets

    The Android app is published on Google Play as WorkPal (package com.workpal.workpal, developer WORKPAL LIMITED, Grove House, 145-149 Donegall Pass, Belfast BT7 1DT). When checked on 25 October 2026 the listing showed version 5.4.5, updated 16 October 2026, with a minimum API level of 30 (Android 11), a target API level of 36, device chips for Phone and Tablet, and 5,000 plus downloads. The release notes for that version mention image upload performance, parts and assets on jobs, and forms on completed jobs. Source: play.google.com

  • Keep the app current: the vendor blames many issues on old versions

    The vendor's mobile user guide says to open the Google Play Store and search for WorkPal, to check for updates if it is already installed, and that many issues we see come down to older versions still being in use. With the Play minimum already at Android 11 and the app targeting API 36, a device with headroom above the floor is less likely to be left behind by a future release. Source: workpal-support.instantdocsbase.com

  • RAM, storage and screen size: not published

    No minimum or recommended RAM, storage or screen size for the WorkPal app was found on the vendor's site, its Google Play listing or its help centre when read on 25 October 2026. The help centre does say to keep the device and apps updated for performance. If your WorkPal account manager gives a device specification, check it against the figures below before you buy. Source: workpal-support.instantdocsbase.com

  • Offline working with an Outbox that syncs when signal returns

    The vendor's mobile app page says the app works even without an internet connection, that teams can fill in forms and capture data offline, and that it syncs once they are back online. The mobile user guide adds that syncing happens automatically in the background, that a connection indicator and an Outbox counter show what is waiting, that if your signal drops the app stores your updates and sends them when the connection returns, that a manual sync is available from the top right menu, and not to close the app while the Outbox is not zero. The vendor does not publish how much is cached on the device or how long a completed job is kept before it is removed. Source: yourworkpal.com

  • Location tracking needs Allow all the time, precise location and Battery Saver off

    The vendor's location permissions article says WorkPal needs access to your device's location for the tracking feature to work. On Android it asks for Allow all the time under the app's Location permission, the device location toggle on and Google Location Accuracy on, and for Battery Saver to be disabled because it can restrict location services and background syncing. The battery usage article recommends using WorkPal with Battery Saver Mode disabled wherever possible, says navigation and location-based apps can significantly increase battery usage when running continuously in the background, and recommends carrying a portable charger or battery pack when working away from a power source for extended periods. Source: workpal-support.instantdocsbase.com

  • Photos from the camera or the gallery, documents, forms and signatures

    The mobile user guide describes taking a photo through Add in the Images section, or pressing and holding Add to pick one from the camera roll, and a newer help article describes an Add Image from Gallery button beside the Camera button for choosing one or more existing images. Forms are completed in the app, read-only PDFs can be attached to a job, and the job is finished with an operative signature and, if required, a customer signature. No barcode, QR or NFC scanning is described, so plan on the camera for photos and nothing more. Source: workpal-support.instantdocsbase.com

  • One device per user, and a mobile login is not a desktop login

    The vendor's guide says each user should log in on one device only, because shared logins can cause syncing problems and missing or duplicated data; the username looks like an email address but does not need to be a real email account, and passwords are system-generated and reset by a desktop administrator. A separate help article says desktop login details will not work on mobile and mobile login details will not work on desktop, and that a user who needs both needs an additional licence. For a shared pool of tablets, that means one WorkPal mobile user per device rather than one login passed around. Source: workpal-support.instantdocsbase.com

  • Windows: no Windows app; the office platform is a web login

    The vendor publishes Android and iOS apps (the App Store listing, read on 25 October 2026, requires iOS 17.6 or iPadOS 17.6 or later and is designed for iPad) and refers to a desktop platform for the office, which its home page links to as a web login. No Windows app and no list of supported browsers or browser versions was found on the vendor's site or help centre. Source: apps.apple.com

Setting up

Getting WorkPal running

  1. Ask your WorkPal administrator to create a mobile user for you. A mobile login is separate from a desktop login and needs its own licence, and the vendor says each user should log in on one device only, so for a shared pool of tablets set up one mobile user per device.
  2. On the Tuga device, open the Google Play Store, search for WorkPal (the listing is by WORKPAL LIMITED, package com.workpal.workpal) and install it. If it is already installed, check for an update: the vendor says many issues come down to older versions still being in use.
  3. Log in with the username your office gives you, which looks like an email address but need not be a real mailbox, and the system-generated password. Only a desktop administrator can reset it.
  4. Grant the permissions the vendor asks for: Settings, Apps, WorkPal, Permissions, Location, Allow all the time; then Settings, Location on with Google Location Accuracy on. Turn Battery Saver off on the device, since the vendor says it can restrict location services and background syncing.
  5. Run a test job before the first real one: tap Start Shift, open a job from the Jobs tile, use Directions and the travel timers, then on site add a note, attach a PDF, complete a form, take a photo and add one from the gallery, and finish with the operative and customer signatures. Watch the connection indicator and the Outbox counter in the app.
  6. Before closing the app at the end of a shift, make sure the Outbox reads zero; trigger a manual sync from the top right menu if it does not. The vendor says a completed job syncs to the office and is removed from the device after a short period, so the device is not your archive.

Questions

WorkPal on a Tuga device

WorkPal's Google Play listing, read on 25 October 2026, sets a minimum of Android 11 with device chips for Phone and Tablet. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12, the A10 Android 14 and the A6 Android 15, all with Google Play, so each meets the published minimum. We have not run WorkPal on these devices ourselves and WorkPal Limited has not certified them, so install the app on one unit and run a test job during the 30-day returns window before buying for the team.

The vendor says the app works without an internet connection, stores your updates if your signal drops and sends them when the connection returns, with an Outbox counter showing what is waiting. That is a property of the app, not the device. What the device adds is dual SIM 4G on the A8, A10 and A6 so the Outbox empties from site rather than from the next Wi-Fi, and enough storage (128GB on the A8 and A10, 64GB plus microSD on the A6) for a day of photos and PDFs waiting to sync.

We do not publish run times, because they depend on screen brightness, signal and how often the app polls location. What the catalogue does list is battery capacity and whether it is removable: 8000mAh removable on the A8, 8000mAh with quick charge but not listed as removable on the A10, and 5050mAh removable on the A6. A removable battery means a charged spare takes over mid shift, which is the vendor's portable charger advice without the cable. The 12V DC Car Charger at £26 fits every model, and the Vehicle Mounting Dock at £109 keeps the A8 or A10 charging on the move.

Not the mobile app: WorkPal publishes it for Android and iOS only. The office side of WorkPal is a desktop web platform, and a desktop login is separate from a mobile login with its own licence, so a W10 in the office could reach that platform in a browser the vendor supports (it publishes no browser list). For the field app, choose an Android device.

WorkPal's published material describes photos, forms, documents, signatures and location tracking, and no barcode, QR or NFC scanning, so plan on none. The A6's built-in 2D scanner and the NFC on every Tuga device are there for other apps you may run alongside WorkPal; ask WorkPal Limited directly if scanning matters to you, as features change.
